name: AI in assessment debate
description: Semester round on the motion "Universities should ban generative AI in graded assessment." The briefing starts at 5:40pm in the foyer and the first speech is at 6:00pm. Each speech is 6 minutes, with one round of points of information. Visitors can sit at the back and do not need to speak. New speakers are paired with an experienced member if they say so at the door. The night ends by 7:30pm. Free for Macquarie students. Bring a student card and a pen.
meetingNote: Theatre foyer, red MQ Debating banner

name: Rapid night and beginner lesson
description: Weekly rapid chess on level 2. A 20-minute lesson for new players and anyone under a 1200 rating starts at 4:40pm. Round one starts at 5:15pm, so be at a board by 5:00pm or you may have to wait for the next round. Each game is 10 minutes plus a 5-second increment. Sets and clocks are provided. The night runs until about 7:00pm. Free for Macquarie students. No rating and no membership are required.
meetingNote: Level 2 group tables, near the stairs

name: Morning skill session
building: 10 Gymnasium Road (Macquarie University Sport and Aquatic Centre)
description: A 45-minute session outside the aquatic centre entrance: pull-up progressions, dips and a short conditioning finisher. It is aimed at beginners. A gym induction is not required and the group does not go into the pool hall. Arrive at 6:50am so names can be checked before the warm-up. Wear training clothes and bring water. The session is free for Macquarie students.
meetingNote: Outside the aquatic centre entrance

name: Past Lives screening
description: A campus screening of Past Lives, then a 15-minute discussion in the same room. Doors open at 6:40pm and the film starts at 7:00pm. Members of Cinema Society get in free. Other Macquarie students pay $5 in cash at the door. Seating is first come and the theatre is not held past the start time. The discussion is optional. Running time is about two hours including the talk.
meetingNote: Price Theatre doors, Cinema Society shirt

name: Open choreography workshop
description: An open workshop on the grass beside the Central Courtyard stage. The hour covers one NewJeans chorus and one aespa chorus, taught from the first eight-count. No audition and no experience. Wear shoes you can turn in and bring a water bottle. The society is not selling drinks. If it rains, the same session moves under the walkway next to the stage and a committee member will be at the original spot until 4:40pm to redirect people.
meetingNote: Grass beside the Central Courtyard stage

name: One-shot games afternoon
description: A one-shot Dungeons & Dragons table and two board-game tables, running about three hours. New players are seated with a host who explains the rules before the first turn. Dice, character sheets and the board games are provided. Bring a student card. The Dungeons & Dragons table takes six players and extra names go on a waiting list at the door. Finish time is about 4:00pm. Free for Macquarie students.
meetingNote: Tutorial room door labelled Tabletop Society

name: Graduate careers panel
description: Three Macquarie graduates speak for 15 minutes each about first jobs in consulting, teaching and public health, then take questions until 1:20pm. Lunch is included: vegetarian and halal sandwiches, labelled at the table. Bring your own cup if you want tea. Aimed at any year, including first years who have not started applying. Sign the attendance sheet if you want the speakers' slides afterwards.
meetingNote: Room booked under Career Advancement Society

name: Concert audition workshop
description: An audition workshop for the end-of-semester concert, then a repertoire rehearsal. All voice parts are welcome, including people who have not sung in a group before. The audition is one short verse, unaccompanied, and takes about two minutes. Sheet music is emailed the day before to anyone who writes to the society by 5:00pm on Saturday 14 November. The afternoon ends at 4:00pm. No fee.
meetingNote: Music room, follow the singing from the lobby

name: Lake to arts lawn photo walk
description: A slow walk from the library lake to the arts lawn while the light is still soft. Any camera or phone is fine. The group makes three stops, and each stop has five minutes to shoot before moving on. At the arts lawn there is a 15-minute critique where people show one frame. Wear shoes for grass and paths. The walk is about 70 minutes. Free, and new members do not need to bring a portfolio.
meetingNote: Library steps on the lake side

name: City screening: Your Name
building: Event Cinemas George Street, 505 George Street, Sydney
description: A group screening of Your Name at Event Cinemas George Street. Buy your own ticket online before Friday 6 November and choose the 6:00pm session so the group can sit together. Meet at 5:15pm in the level 1 foyer. From Macquarie University station, allow about 40 minutes by Metro and a city train, and get off at Town Hall. After the film, anyone who wants to walks to a casual dinner nearby. Dinner is not booked and everyone pays for themselves. This is a student meetup, not a cinema promotion.
meetingNote: Level 1 foyer, Anime MQ sign

name: General insurance briefing
description: The society's one briefing this month. Two Macquarie graduates who now work in general insurance cover pricing, claims and the graduate application dates for 2027. Arrive by 5:20pm. The talk is 50 minutes and questions run for 15 minutes, finishing at 6:35pm. Free for Macquarie students. Bring a student card. Slides are emailed the next day to people who sign the sheet. No internship is required.
meetingNote: Level 1 seminar room booked under Actuarial Students Society

name: Clerkship information night
description: A night for students applying for summer clerkships. A recent clerk explains the online application, the interview and what a typical week looked like. Doors open at 5:45pm. The talk starts at 6:00pm and questions go to 7:00pm. Aimed at penultimate-year law students, and earlier years can sit in. Bring a copy of your CV if you want five minutes of written comments afterwards. The first 20 CVs are read on the night.
meetingNote: Lecture room booked under Law Society

name: Jollof supper
description: A shared supper on the courtyard. Jollof, plantain and a vegetarian pot are served from 6:00pm until the trays are finished, usually about 7:15pm. Macquarie students eat free. Friends from outside the university pay $5 at the table. Bring your own cup and a container if you want to take a second serving away. The society will have halal meat in a separate tray, labelled.
meetingNote: Central Courtyard, tables under the African Society banner

name: Language exchange and calligraphy
description: Forty minutes of paired Japanese and English conversation, then a short calligraphy table. Beginners are paired with a speaker. You do not need to know hiragana. Brushes and paper are provided for the first 25 people. The session is on level 2 and stays quiet enough for the library. It ends at 5:30pm. Free for Macquarie students.
meetingNote: Level 2 group tables, Japanese Association sign

name: Social hit and beginner drills
building: 10 Gymnasium Road (Macquarie University Sport and Aquatic Centre)
description: Court hire is already paid. The first 30 minutes are feeder drills for beginners, then social games until 8:30pm. Racquets and shuttles are provided, and you can bring your own racquet. Non-marking indoor shoes are required. The sports centre front desk will turn away outdoor shoes. Free for Macquarie students. Put your name down by 7:10pm or your place on a court may be given away.
meetingNote: Indoor courts, ask the front desk for Badminton Club

name: Cleaning a real dataset
description: A two-hour workshop using a public transport-delay spreadsheet. You will find missing values, fix dates and make one chart. Bring a laptop with a browser. Python is not required. The room has power points along the side wall, so a charger is worth bringing. Starts at 5:00pm sharp and ends at 7:00pm. Aimed at first and second years. Free.
meetingNote: Computer lab door labelled AI and Data Science Society

name: Bridge-build afternoon
description: Teams of three build a small bridge from paddle-pop sticks and glue, then test it with a bucket of water bottles. Materials are provided. Teams are made at the door if you come alone. The build runs from 1:00pm to 2:30pm and the test takes about 20 minutes. Closed shoes are required because sticks snap. Free for Macquarie students in any faculty, not only engineering.
meetingNote: Ground-floor workshop space, Engineering Society banner

name: Diwali evening on the courtyard
description: Diwali falls on Sunday 8 November. The society is holding a short lighting, sweets and music on the courtyard from 5:00pm to 7:00pm. Sweets are vegetarian and labelled for nuts. Candles stay inside holders and are put out by 7:00pm. Open to every student. No cost and no dress code. If you want to help set out the tables, come at 4:30pm and find the Hindu Society sign.
meetingNote: Central Courtyard, Hindu Society sign by the stage

name: Pitch night for the next issue
description: Editors hear story ideas for the next print issue. Bring a one-paragraph pitch, or write it on the sheet at the door. Each person gets three minutes, and the editors say yes, no or rewrite before the next pitch. The issue deadline they are working to is the last week of November. New writers are welcome and do not need a portfolio. Starts at 6:00pm and the list usually finishes by 7:30pm.
meetingNote: Meeting room, Grapeshot copies on the table

name: Kamayan picnic
description: A shared picnic lunch. Rice, grilled vegetables and a meat tray are laid out for people to eat with their hands if they want to. Plates and forks are there as well. Macquarie students eat free. The meat tray is separate from the vegetarian food. Bring a hat if you are sitting in the sun, and a container if you want leftovers. Serving starts at 12:00pm and packing up is at 1:30pm.
meetingNote: Courtyard lawn, Filipino Students Society blanket

name: First pull request
description: A practical hour for students who have not opened a pull request before. Tutors walk through cloning a small class repository, changing one file and opening the request. Bring a laptop with a GitHub account already created. If you do not have an account, make one before 6:00pm because the room wifi is slow at the start of the hour. Ends at 7:15pm. Free, and you do not need to be in a computing unit.
meetingNote: Lab door labelled Association of Computing Students

name: Campus creek survey
description: A one-hour walk from the library lake along the campus creek to note birds, litter and water clarity. Clipboards and a one-page ID sheet are provided. You do not need biology knowledge. Wear closed shoes that can handle wet grass and bring water. The group leaves the library steps at 9:10am, so arrive before then. Notes from the walk are sent to the society's next meeting. They are not a formal university survey.
meetingNote: Library steps on the lake side, BEES clipboard

name: Lunchtime rates talk
description: A 40-minute talk on how an interest-rate decision reaches rents and graduate jobs, using the latest public Reserve Bank material. No textbook is required. Questions run until 1:15pm so people can get to a 1:30pm class. Free. Bring lunch if you want to eat during the talk. The room is a seminar room, not a lecture hall, and spare seats are released at 12:35pm.
meetingNote: Seminar room booked under Economics Society

name: Welcome walk across campus
description: Student members lead a 40-minute walk on paved paths from the courtyard to the library lake and back, stopping to talk about places they use on campus. It is open to every student. There is no cost and nothing to bring except comfortable shoes. The group leaves at 1:10pm. The walk is not a formal university tour and it does not go inside buildings.
meetingNote: Central Courtyard, Indigenous Student Association sign

name: Placement stories panel
description: Three students who finished a health placement this year speak for 10 minutes each about applications, what to pack and what they wish they had asked. Questions go until 6:40pm. Relevant for health, psychology and allied-health students, and other faculties can attend. Free. A one-page checklist is printed and left by the door.
meetingNote: Seminar room booked under Global Health Society

name: Line-follower test night
description: Bring a robot or use one of the club kits to run a taped line on the lab floor. Kits are limited to eight and are handed out at 6:00pm. If you bring your own robot, it needs to run from a battery and stay under 30 centimetres wide. The test track is taped down before the start and left until 8:00pm. Soldering is not part of this night. Free for Macquarie students.
meetingNote: Lab door labelled Robotics Club

name: Open salsa social
description: A beginner salsa lesson from 6:00pm to 6:40pm, then social dancing until 8:00pm. Partners are rotated, so you can come alone. Smooth-soled shoes are better than runners. Water is available in the foyer. No fee and no audition. The lesson covers a basic step and one turn. People who already dance can arrive at 6:40pm for the social half.
meetingNote: Lotus Theatre foyer, Dance Club speaker

name: Monday breakfast before class
description: Toast, fruit and tea from 8:00am to 8:45am for anyone with a morning class. Food is free. Vegetarian options are on a separate plate. You do not need to stay for any talk. The society packs up at 8:45am so the courtyard is clear before 9:00am classes. Bring your own cup if you have one.
meetingNote: Central Courtyard, Christian Union table by the stage
